985.body: Two games can cost the same, promise the same top prize, and still be totally different animals. "MAX-A-MILLION" is a grinder — it pays out lots of smaller prizes instead of a few monsters — most of its unclaimed prize money sits in wins under $5,000, with the rest stacked up top. Neither style is "better." They're just built for different players. If you're a regular on this game, bookmark it — this write-up refreshes with every morning's data.

993.body: "$5,000 Triple Play" keeps doing the most interesting thing a scratcher can do: nothing. The $5,000 top prizes haven't been hit for three months, while the everyday prizes keep getting claimed out of an ever-smaller stack of tickets. They printed a fixed number of these — every quiet day tightens that math a little more. Everything above comes from the North Carolina Lottery's own published numbers — we just do the counting.
